messages:
mira: Heads up — the change to package exports in the js-sdk landed and it's breaking the local edge runner + sample app onboarding. Repro below, tagging @jon for runtime parity and @kevin for packaging.

mira: Repro steps:
1) clone examples/nextjs-starter
2) yarn && yarn dev
3) open localhost -> console shows import error

mira: package.json exports we pushed:
```json
{
  \"name\": \"@redwood/js-sdk\",
  \"exports\": {
    \".\": {
      \"node\": \"./dist/node/index.js\",
      \"default\": \"./dist/edge/index.mjs\"
    },
    \"./server\": \"./dist/server/index.js\"
  }
}
```

mira: Error in dev console (wrangler / vite):
```
Error [ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED]: No \"exports\" main defined for package '/.../node_modules/@redwood/js-sdk'
    at new NodeError (node:internal/errors:371:5)
    at packageExportsResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:550:9)
    at resolveExports (node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:583:11)
    at resolvePackageTarget (node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:710:10)
    at resolvePackage (node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:773:10)
```

jon: Ugh, this smells like conditional exports + bundler/runtime mismatch. Some runtimes (wrangler/esbuild/vite in worker mode) won't pick up the `default` target the way Node does. Did we include an `import` conditional or `.mjs` vs `.js` variants?

mira: We shipped the edge build as `.mjs` and used `default` for the edge path. Node consumers pick `node` key, bundlers sometimes look for `import` or `default` differently.

kevin: Quick thought: we probably need to add an explicit `import` condition in the exports to cover ESM bundlers, and also provide a fallback `./dist/edge/index.js` (non-.mjs) for tools that don't like .mjs. Example:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/edge/index.js",
    "node": "./dist/node/index.js",
    "default": "./dist/edge/index.js"
  }
}
```

kevin: Also add "types": "./dist/index.d.ts" at package root so TS pickers don't try to reach into dist subpaths.

sam: Short-term workaround for samples: import deep path from dist: `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/js-sdk/dist/edge/index.js'`. Not ideal but unblocks onboarding.

sam: Longer term we should:
- revert the export change and publish a patch to avoid breaking new users
- add a smoke test that runs our samples against wrangler/vite/esbuild/bun locally
- add docs on how exports should be structured for edge-compatible SDKs

mira: Agreed. I'll open a PR to revert and add a follow-up that updates exports to include `import`/`.js` fallbacks + tests.

jon: Also check our CI matrix — I don't see edge runner tests covering the sample apps. We should add a job that runs `examples/*` under `wrangler dev --local` or at least a bundler build check.

kevin: Minor gotcha: consumers using `node --trace-warnings` sometimes hit different resolution paths; prefer explicit `import` conditional over `default` for ESM-first packages.

mira: Created issue: #4321 (exports/edge-onboarding-breaks). PR to revert incoming (will mark as hotfix). Will post link when ready.

release-bot: Published hotfix @redwood/js-sdk v0.3.1 -> reverted exports change. Changelog: "fix: make package exports compatible with edge bundlers; temporary revert to unblock samples" :tada:

sam: Thanks — updating sample app to deep import as interim and will add a note in the onboarding doc.

jon: Once hotfix lands let's schedule a short postmortem in eng-devex to pick the long-term export policy. No more surprises between node/bundlers/edge.

mira: +1. Adding action items to the issue. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
